build.title: Approval rules: Save and Apply the default don't work from the Phone Connect app

said.text: Found live with Brett, Nov 21, in the Phone Connect app on his phone (Builds → VPS Configuration → Approval rules, shipped by PR #885). (1) Tapping 'Apply the default' staged nothing: the tab still showed zero rules and Save stayed disabled. Staging the same default through gate/approval-rules-stage {op: default} worked and lit Save. (2) Tapping Save with that draft does nothing visible: the draft stays ('Unsaved changes, last staged by console token'), default.applied stays false, live rules stay empty on axHub, canSave is true. Suspect: the save is sent from the browser on Brett's own axHub session and the app's WebView has no hub session (or the cross-origin request is blocked), and the failure is swallowed with no message. Brett's rule stands: only his own click applies the policy.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Fable phase. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step approval-rules-save-apply-default-don-t <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.

- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.

open: Not run on the phone. No device or Android toolchain here. The cause is from the code of both apps and the WebView's behaviour; the fix on the tab does not depend on that reading being right, because the tab no longer uses a browser dialog at all and every failure path now shows its reason. `JsDialogs` (the overlay dialog) is compiled and unit-tested by CI but was not seen on a screen.
